subject: Pilot SLA: uptime targets, credit cap, and fallback playbook
messages:
From: Laura Stevens <laura.stevens@orbitalai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@orbitalai.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLA baseline and credit questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team liked the predictable latency profile for short chat workloads. Before we turn on the pilot, our legal and procurement teams want a short SLA that covers: standard uptime %, latency SLO for 95th percentile, and the monthly service credit mechanics if the SLA is missed.

Two asks from our side:
- We prefer a 99.95% uptime guarantee for the pilot.
- Given this is a pilot, procurement will only accept a monthly credit cap at 10% of invoice (they want to avoid large credit exposures).

Can you send over a short SLA template (1–2 pages) that shows the credit bands and any carve-outs (maintenance, force majeure, regional outages)? Also: how do you handle temporary degraded throughput (we care about request throttling more than total downtime).

If you can get something over by EOD Wednesday that would be great — procurement moved faster than expected.

Best,
Laura
Laura Stevens
Head of Cloud Architecture
OrbitalAI

--
Attachments: none

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Stevens <laura.stevens@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA baseline and credit questions

Laura —

Thanks for the clear asks. I've attached a focused SLA draft that mirrors Redwood's standard pilot terms but with two areas we usually negotiate: 1) standard uptime floor and credit tiers, and 2) a degraded-throughput fallback where we route to a compatible lower-throughput variant instead of issuing immediate credits.

Key points in the attached SLA_Draft_Orbital_v1.pdf:
- Baseline uptime: 99.9% (monthly).
- Credit bands:
  * >=99.9% — no credits
  * 99.5%–99.9% — 5% of monthly invoice
  * 99.0%–99.5% — 15% of monthly invoice
  * <99.0% — 30% of monthly invoice
- Monthly credit cap: 20% of invoice for pilots (we can consider 10% for multi-month commitments).
- Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows (we propose a rolling 6-hour/month maintenance allowance), emergency maintenance (notification within 2 hours), force majeure.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency target for the configured model; credits are driven by availability, not microbursts.
- Fallback playbook: when request queueing exceeds thresholds or the model variant is unavailable, traffic is smoothly shifted to a lower-cost/quantized model for up to 60 minutes before credits are considered. The playbook includes customer notification hooks and optional throttling settings.

I've kept the draft intentionally permissive on the monthly cap because we typically avoid very low caps for short pilots — they can make fallback behavior too risky on our side. But happy to mark an explicit pilot exception to get you started if procurement insists.

Attachment: SLA_Draft_Orbital_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Cheers,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
priom_das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Laura Stevens <laura.stevens@orbitalai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@orbitalai.com
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA baseline and credit questions

Priyom —

Appreciate the quick turn. I reviewed the draft and flagged changes (attached redlines). A few notes from procurement / legal:

1) Baseline uptime — Orbital is asking for 99.95% for the pilot. We accept fallback variants but only if credits are not delayed beyond the same monthly reconciliation window. In other words, fallback is fine but it doesn't delay credit eligibility.
2) Credit cap — procurement is firm at 10% for this pilot. They view any higher cap as creating large downside during evaluation.
3) Maintenance carve-out — fine, but scheduled maintenance cannot exceed 4 hours/month for pilot.
4) Latency — we want the 95th pct token latency target documented with a sample measurement window and the model name used for measurement.

I've attached redlines (redlines-20260923.docx). If you can't accept 10% cap, please propose a compromise path (e.g., 10% month 1, 15% thereafter or a time-boxed cap upgrade tied to usage).

Thanks,
Laura

Attachments: redlines-20260923.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Stevens <laura.stevens@orbitalai.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA baseline and credit questions

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the redlines. Looping in Ben to give input on the credit cap and payment exposure. A quick internal summary of our suggested compromise:

- Pilot month 1: 10% cap (to match Orbital procurement).
- Conditional increase: If Orbital > $50k usage in month 2, cap becomes 15% starting month 2. This avoids large tail risk while giving room for scale.
- Uptime: We can accept 99.95% for the pilot only if Orbital agrees to a 90-minute aggregated maintenance allowance per quarter (we'll log and notify). Alternatively we can document an explicit degraded-throughput SLA where credits are reduced by 50% if the fallback playbook was invoked for < 30 minutes in the month.
- Latency measurement: We'll include model ID and a 7-day rolling measurement window for the 95th pct; this will be included as an appendix.

Ben — do you want to add product/ops notes on the fallback playbook (timeouts, notification cadence, acceptable throughput reduction)?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Global Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Laura Stevens <laura.stevens@orbitalai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, contracts@orbitalai.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 16:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA baseline and credit questions

Marissa, Priyom —

Thanks for the proposed compromise. The conditional cap path (10% month 1, 15% after usage threshold) is acceptable to procurement provided we capture it in the SLA and include a simple monthly reconciliation example.

We also accept the degraded-throughput fallback as long as:
- Credits are reduced (by 50%) only when fallback was invoked < 30 minutes in the month (as you suggested).
- If fallback was used > 30 minutes, credits are calculated against the availability bands without the reduction.

Please send a final redlined PDF and a DocuSign-ready version so our legal team can sign the pilot addendum.

I'll loop in contracts@orbitalai.com to get signatures queued.

Best,
Laura
Laura Stevens
Head of Cloud Architecture
OrbitalAI

--
Attachments: none
